To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the decay schemes of neutron-deficient Rh and Ru isotopes were extended and new isomers in Rh were identified.
the $\gamma$ decay of the low-spin isomerase of 92Rh has been identified for the first-time.
we have studied the $\beta$-decay of the very neutron-deficient isotopes 90,91,92,92m,93Rh and the $\beta$ decay of 90,92Ru.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the decay properties of neutron-deficient Rh and Ru nuclei.
the study of the structure of neutron-deficient nuclei in the region of the Z = 28 shell gap, using $\beta$-decay spectroscopy.
the study of the very neutron-deficient rhodiuim and ruthenium nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the decay of the neutron-deficient 89-92Ru and 89-93Rh isotopes was studied and the results were compared to theoretical calculations.
the $\beta$-decay properties of these nuclei are consistent with the shell-model calculations.
the experimental data are in excellent agreement with theoretical predictions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to establish the $\beta$-decay scheme of 91Rh, the $\beta$ decay and the isomerism of 92Rh and the $\beta$ decays of 90,93Ru.
the decay schemes for the neutron-deficient rhium and ruthenium nuclei are now well established and the decay of the very neutron-deficient rhidium isotopes has been investigated in detail.
the $\beta$-decay of these neutron-deficient nuclei are dominated by the $\nu$g7/2 proton orbital and the decay schemes are in good agreement with the results of shell model calculations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the $\beta$-decay properties of these very neutron-deficient isotopes are consistent with the predictions of shell-model calculations, and in particular the low-spin $\beta$-decays in the Ru isotopes are consistent within uncertainties.
we were able to identify a number of new decay paths in neutron-deficient Rh and Ru isotopes.
the $\gamma$ decaying isomers of the 92Rh and 91Ru isotopes have low spins and that the low-spin isomer of 92Rh is most likely a $1/2^-$ state.
